title: "D9 reversed: devbin requires bash >= 5 and refuses older, rather than targeting 3.2"
body:
# 0022: D9 reversed: devbin requires bash >= 5 and refuses older, rather than targeting 3.2

## Tags

bash, floor, D9, dispatcher, doctor, ci, ruling

## Summary

hv's ruling, 2026-08-24, on being shown doctor's "devbin targets 3.2" note: the bash that actually runs devbin everywhere in this fleet is Homebrew's 5.x (`type bash` -> /opt/homebrew/bin/bash, 5.3.15 at ruling time), so the guarantee should point at what runs -- require a current bash and ensure it -- not at the stock `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 that Apple froze permanently over GPLv3. Floor chosen: **major >= 5** (robust across brew versions and Linux CI, rather than tracking brew's current minor).

D9's original ground is unchanged and recorded in `design.md` beside the reversal note: 3.2 targeting bought stock-Mac bootstrap (a launcher that works before brew exists) and a CI leg that caught bash-4+ constructs. The reversal trades the bootstrap case away deliberately -- a fresh Mac now gets a clear refusal with remediation instead of a working launcher -- because every machine this fleet runs on carries brew bash, and the dialect tax (no `declare -A`, no `mapfile`, guarded array expansion) was being paid for a case that never occurs here.

## Reproduction

Of the new behavior, both directions, measured at implementation time:

    /bin/bash bin/devbin --version   -> exit 1: "devbin: bash >= 5 is required; this is bash 3.2.57(1)-release (/bin/bash)"
                                        + "brew install bash" remediation
    bin/devbin --version             -> exit 0 (env bash resolves brew 5.3.15)

The refusal test in `tests/unit/dispatch.bats` was run BEFORE the guard existed and failed (dispatcher accepted 3.2, printed a version) -- the red-check -- then passed after.

## Root Cause

Not a defect; a scope ruling. Recorded as an issue because hv ruled issues are the mechanism and no steel thread is warranted.

## Impact

- `bin/devbin` gains the floor guard immediately after `set -euo pipefail` -- one home, everything else (sourced libs, handlers as child processes re-entering via the dispatcher) is behind it. The guard block itself stays parseable by bash 3.2 so the refusal cannot arrive as a syntax error.
- `doctor`'s bash row inverts from note to check: PASS naming the version under the floor, FAIL with remediation below it -- the check that goes red if the dispatcher guard is ever removed.
- `usage-rules.md` Shell section rewritten: the 3.2 bans drop; existing 3.2 idioms (guarded expansion, case-over-associative-array) stay as harmless and are modernised opportunistically, never in bulk; the `&`-in-replacement rule SURVIVES because bash 5.2 changed it and a >= 5 floor still spans 5.0/5.1 (literal) and 5.2+ (matched text).
- CI's macOS job inverts: it now installs brew bash, asserts PATH bash meets the floor before running the suite, and PROVES the refusal against the runner's real /bin/bash 3.2 -- the one runner that always carries an old bash. Without that job the refusal test in dispatch.bats would skip forever on >= 5 platforms.
- Tests: the old full-stack-under-3.2 dispatch test became the refusal test plus a floor-compliant positive twin; run_referent.bats's seven `/bin/bash` dispatcher invocations became direct invocations (their subject is referents, not bash vintage); the surfaces.bats repl fixture's narrowed PATH gains a >= 5 bash symlink (a stripped PATH resolving `env bash` to /bin/bash now means refusal -- found by the suite, not by inspection); helpers.bats's 3.2 empty-array measurements stay as recorded history of what the idiom protected against.
- zsh: untouched and irrelevant -- zsh 5.9 is the interactive shell and never executes devbin.

## Proposed Fix

Implemented with the filing; the fleet takes it at the next `devbin upgrade` sweep, after which every install refuses old bash the same way. Until a given install is swept it still runs the old dispatcher and merely lacks the guard -- nothing breaks in the interim.

## Related

- ST0001 `design.md` D9 -- carries the dated reversal note beside the original reasoning
- 0021 -- the other upgrade-adjacent refinements from the same day's audit
- cc/wip.md watch-out on `[ -nt ]` whole-second ties -- an example of the 3.2/5.x span-bug class the floor retires

## Resolutions

**CLOSED 2026-08-24 (vc).** Implemented, proven, swept and landed the same day hv ruled it.

- Devbin `7213128`: the dispatcher guard, doctor's check, the usage-rules rewrite, D9's dated reversal note, the CI inversion, and the three fixture repairs. The refusal test was run against the guard-less dispatcher FIRST and failed -- the red-check -- then passed. Suite 588 ok / 0 failed / bats rc 0 on a quiet tree (the first attempt was contaminated by this session's own mid-run edits, which is the project's own probe-a-tree-mid-run rule biting its author).
- Fleet: all ten installs re-swept, 8 files each, zero skips, doctor green both sides, every manifest stamped `7213128` clean, and a per-install probe confirming the guard LIVE (`/bin/bash bin/<prj>` refuses) rather than merely delivered. Landed: Conflab `24e2240a`, Laksa `cfe6709d2`, Baize `2585d21`, Lamplight `a09620e4b`, MicroGPTEx `0c373f3`, arca_config `1d9e773`, arca_cli `f157ca6`, Prolix `c3e2027`, Riffle `556115a`, Intent `ad0ba20d`.
- Owner-verified independently at Lamplight (footprint, refusal probe, doctor 10/0) and Baize (both suites green, both arms of the guard).

**What the sweep protocol gained, and it is the durable half.** A behaviour-changing sweep now brackets the coupled consumer suite where one exists, asks the RUNNER what it collects rather than listing a directory, and probes the delivered behaviour per install. The reason is measured: sweep #1's report was accurate on every claim and Baize's shell suite was red from the moment it landed, because a vendored contract change (runlog's keep-newest-N purge) broke a NON-vendored consumer test -- outside any per-file replace and any skip-list. Doctor green measures the framework's health, not whether the consumer still works.

**Coverage fact found on the way, tracked against 0019:** Conflab and Lamplight have no consumer-side runlog coverage at all, so the next contract change lands there silently.
